definitions.note: a divine is a noun here, a clergyman or theologian

indicators.note: vicious suggests something savage and wild, so the letters of circle are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone describes a vicious circle, the trap of problems feeding each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vicious circle' reads as a fixed phrase, but 'vicious' is the anagram signal for CIRCLE, and 'Divine' is a noun, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A divine is a priest or theologian, and a cleric is a member of the clergy.

parts.note: to lie is to invent a falsehood

indicators.note: the word for information goes about, around, the state's abbreviation

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
MA is the abbreviation for Massachusetts, a US state

explanation.surface: Someone makes up news about a country's dependent territory.
explanation.definitionFit: A liegeman was a vassal owing service to his feudal lord, so a dependant.

clue.text: Extravagant work shop with yard being built

indicators.note: something being built is being assembled from parts, so the letters are put together anew

explanation.surface: Lavish building works on a shop and its yard.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhapsody is an effusive, free-form musical or literary composition.

clue.text: Low-voiced woman Liberal to support the other side

indicators.note: in a down clue the pieces that support another sit beneath it

parts.note: contra means against, on the opposing side

explanation.surface: A woman in the Liberal party decides to back the opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: A contralto is the lowest female singing voice, or the singer with it.

clue.text: Investor in ring not expected to do well

explanation.surface: A gambler bets in a boxing or betting ring on someone nobody fancies.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'ring' is the closed circle of stock-exchange members or bookmakers; an investor who is not a member of it was once called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is an investor dealing from beyond the closed trading circle; the other is a horse or contender given little chance of winning.

clue.text: Too much growth presents a dark picture

explanation.surface: Overbuilding makes for a gloomy outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is photographic: film left too long in developer gives a dark image.
explanation.definitionFit: It is excessive expansion, and in photography too long in developer, which makes the print or negative too dark.

indicators.note: the word for artful forms surroundings, wrapping round the gallery's name

parts.note: sly means artful, cunning
the Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.surface: A grand gallery is set in artistically designed grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Stately means imposing and dignified, as grand does.

explanation.surface: A boarding-school master who runs a boarding house in the town of Beaconsfield.
explanation.walkthrough: Benjamin Disraeli, British prime minister, was made Earl of Beaconsfield; as leader of the House of Commons he was its master.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian premier took the title Earl of Beaconsfield, and he dominated the House of Commons as its leader.

clue.text: Best place to see band off, perhaps

parts.note: a ring is a circular band
in cricket the off is one side of the field, so off is an example of a side

explanation.surface: Where to stand to watch a band set off.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat right by a boxing ring gives the closest view of a fight.

clue.text: Captive Basque nationalists in hiding in the river

indicators.note: something hiding in a place is tucked inside it, so these pieces go within the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland, and another in Wales and England, a crossword staple
ETA was the Basque separatist group in Spain

explanation.surface: A Basque separatist prisoner lies low somewhere by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Captive' is a noun here, a prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: A detainee is someone held in custody, a prisoner.

parts.note: to dam water is to hold it back, so holds back gives dams

explanation.surface: Someone restrains themselves from eating fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The damson is a small dark plum, a kind of fruit.

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, which crosswords treat as many

indicators.note: the word for doubtless sits inside the word for extremity

parts.note: an extremity is an end
doubtless means sure, certain

explanation.surface: Many were doomed, no doubt, in a time of dire extremity.
explanation.definitionFit: To censure is to criticise severely, so condemned and censured are synonyms.

clue.text: Ribbons for a damsel in distress

indicators.note: a thing in distress is damaged or broken up, so the letters of damsel are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ribbons are offered to a fairytale damsel in distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damsel in distress' reads as a stock phrase; 'in distress' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Military decorations hang from ribbons, and 'ribbons' is used for the awards themselves.

parts.note: de is French for of
a livery is a servant's or company's uniform

explanation.surface: A French uniform is handed over in a surrender.
explanation.definitionFit: Delivery can mean the formal handing over of property or of a place, a surrender.

clue.text: Inward looking new boy, pursuing religious education

indicators.note: a piece pursuing another comes after it

parts.note: RE is the school subject Religious Education
an entrant is a newcomer, someone just joining

explanation.surface: A shy new pupil follows a scripture lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: A re-entrant angle points inwards, as in a fortification's inward-facing corner.

explanation.surface: Two words of qualification placed side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Only means merely or solely, and as a conjunction it means but, except that.

clue.text: Angry, not being in fashion with many

parts.note: out is the opposite of in
the rage is the current fashion
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred, so many

explanation.surface: Someone is furious at being out of step with fashion and the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Outraged means deeply offended and furious.

clue.text: Exponent first in charge of military organisation

parts.note: a logarithm is an exponent in mathematics, shortened to log
1st, written IST, is first

explanation.surface: A leading proponent in charge of army planning.
explanation.definitionFit: Logistics is the planning of supply and movement of troops, so logistic relates to that organisation.

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the letters picked out are read backwards
from signals that the letters are taken out of the inside of the word remedial

explanation.surface: An assistant gives up remedial teaching to retire.
explanation.walkthrough: The run EDIA sits inside 'remedial'; 'retiring' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide is a helper or assistant, especially to an official.

clue.text: Senators confused by parliamentary candidate's need for his endorsement

definitions.text: parliamentary candidate's need for his endorsement

indicators.note: confused letters are mixed up, so the letters of senators are reordered

explanation.surface: Senators are baffled by a candidate seeking endorsement.
explanation.walkthrough: In British elections a candidate's nomination paper needs the signatures of several local voters, who give their assent.
explanation.definitionFit: A British nomination paper needs signatures from electors who agree to back the nominee.

parts.note: des is French for some
cents are coins, money

explanation.surface: A French person turns down some money.
explanation.definitionFit: Descents are downward slopes or falls, so declines.

parts.note: in football an end can be a goal, so a draw with no goals scored is described as having no end

explanation.definitionFit: A football draw where neither side scores is a nil-nil game, with no goals at either end.

clue.text: I'm in favour of unpleasant expression

indicators.note: the letters of I'm sit inside the word for favour

parts.note: grace means favour, as in being in someone's good graces

explanation.surface: Someone declares themselves in favour of something unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: A grimace is a twisted facial look of disgust or pain.

clue.text: Dried grape is in the water

indicators.note: the word is sits inside the word for the water

parts.note: rain is water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: A dried grape is soaking in water.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a grape dried in the sun or by machine.

clue.text: "How poor are they that have not ____" (Othello)

definitions.text: "How poor are they that have not ____" (Othello)

parts.words: "How poor are they that have not ____" (Othello)
parts.note: a quotation with a missing word: Iago tells Othello that people lacking a calm, enduring quality are poor

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation from Shakespeare's Othello, Act 2, where Iago adds that wounds heal only by degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: The quoted line praises forbearance: those lacking calm endurance are poor in spirit.

parts.note: got can mean fetched or brought
ham is cured pork, a meat

explanation.surface: The Magi arrived bearing meat instead of gold, frankincense and myrrh.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Wise men of Gotham' are English folklore: villagers of Gotham, Nottinghamshire, who feigned foolishness, so the definition is ironic.
explanation.definitionFit: Folklore's village of fools in Nottinghamshire is famous for its so-called wise men, who acted daft to deter a king.

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
acting means in operation, operative

explanation.surface: A former secret agent is a demanding taskmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Exacting means demanding great care and precision, which is what rigorous means.

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: An ailing pet cried out in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Decrepit means weakened by age or illness, which is to be infirm.

explanation.surface: A political party's whip, the person who enforces voting discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a thrash is a lively party.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrash is informal British for a lively celebration, and to thrash is to beat with a whip or stick.
